questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I mainly chose my study destination because it is a city filled with young students and a lively atmosphere. I was also excited to experience a university that is very well respected there. Additionally, it is an English-speaking country while also being in the French-speaking part of Canada, which felt a bit more European. And of course, Canada’s nature is absolutely amazing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The university is clearly experienced in receiving a large number of exchange students, which was evident throughout the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of helpful emails with important information, including key deadlines, details about the first week of classes, and activities beyond studying.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find off-campus housing. I found a place through Airbnb and shared it with four other girls from UCPH. It wasn’t too expensive, and it worked out really well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I didn’t realize that on-campus housing is often with much younger, first-year students, so I was really happy living off campus. I’d recommend areas like Plateau or Mile-End. Downtown is also close to campus but usually more expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McGill University had an add/drop period during the first two weeks of the semester, which allowed students to try different courses before making a final decision. That worked very well.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at the host institution was relatively easy and straightforward through their online platform. We were given access to the registration system at the beginning of June, and the steps were clear and simple to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Clear and helpful university website and easy access to administrative support

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I was not very successful in registering for the classes I initially wanted. Although I had received prior approval for several courses before arrival, many of them were already full. Local students are given access to course registration approximately two weeks before international students, which meant that many courses were fully booked by the time I was able to register.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting approval for lots of courses early. That way, if a course isn’t offered or is full, you can quickly switch to something else.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took economics courses at the 400 level. Overall, I experienced that the level was somewhat lower than at KU. Several of the topics had already been covered during my first and second year in Denmark. However, I think the teaching style and course content were different enough that it is difficult to make a direct comparison. I was challenged in a different way than I would have been at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style varied between my courses. One felt similar to UCPH with lectures and written exams. Another included participation, assignments, and quizzes, which I wasn’t used to. Both courses had midterms during the semester, which I liked because it eased the pressure on the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 420 Topics in Economic Theory
ECON 440 Health Economics
ECON 408 Public Sector Economics 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend ECON 440 Health Economics. It was not very technical and focused more on discussion. The assignments were policy briefs, and the readings were interesting research articles rather than heavy theory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don’t think I encountered any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was generally a bit more expensive than in Denmark, but overall prices were similar. Public transport was cheaper than expected. You could rent unlimited bikes for just over 100 DKK per month, and a student metro pass was about 250 DKK per month. We also joined the university gym, which cost only around 300 DKK for the entire semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were lots of activities for students. They had a gym and weekly sports like ice skating, yoga, and tennis. They also did fun city tours (like a “bagel tour”). I went on a trip with the McGill Outdoors Club too. One thing I wouldn’t recommend is the first camping trip - mostly very new and much younger students signed up.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Weekly sports, watch a hockey match

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ottawa, Toronto, Québec City (recommend going in December during Christmas). During fall break I went to the Rocky Mountains for about 10 days which I would really recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the local culture. Many students in the classes didn’t know each other very well, so people were friendly and open to talking.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people during classes and participate in events. Joining weekly sports activities is also a good way to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You don’t need to speak fluent French, but sometimes, for example in supermarkets, you would meet people who couldn’t speak English. That could be challenging at times.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how friendly and welcoming Canadians are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be flexible with course registration, join activities early to meet people and take advantage of add/drop period during the first two weeks.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Discovering a new way of studying and living, and getting to know a different culture while making friends from all over.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was getting the courses I wanted. The registration itself was easy, but I had limited flexibility in getting certain courses approved, which made it more difficult to secure the classes I really wanted.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
